cluster_summary: The cluster contains Java deserialization vulnerabilities where untrusted byte streams are passed to ObjectInputStream.readObject() (or Kryo) without any class allowlisting or type filtering, allowing arbitrary gadget-chain execution. Fix strategies vary: applying class allowlists via resolveClass or ObjectInputFilter, replacing native deserialization with manual parsing of primitive types, or removing the serializable classes entirely. One outlier is a JVM termination via System.exit, not a deserialization issue; another outlier has an incomplete fix that does not address the vulnerability.
guideline_text: Trace untrusted serialized bytes, object streams, pickles, marshaled payloads, or type metadata into deserializers that instantiate classes, reconstruct object graphs, or invoke callbacks during object creation. Report code paths where allowed classes, object types, and construction side effects are not constrained before deserialization. Confirm that the guard is enforced before the sensitive effect and remains bound to the same resource, principal, destination, or object that the effect uses. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 18 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should use type allowlists, safe codecs, signature checks, or data-only formats instead of general object deserialization.

mechanism.missing_guard: allowed classes, object types, and construction side effects are not constrained before deserialization
mechanism.name: untrusted deserialization with attacker-controlled type graph
mechanism.sink_shape: deserializers that instantiate classes, reconstruct object graphs, or invoke callbacks during object creation
mechanism.source_shape: untrusted serialized bytes, object streams, pickles, marshaled payloads, or type metadata
mechanism.typical_fix: use type allowlists, safe codecs, signature checks, or data-only formats instead of general object deserialization

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Override resolveClass to check a static allowlist of permitted class names, or set an ObjectInputFilter that rejects any class not in the allowlist. Throw a SecurityException for disallowed classes.
sub_patterns.name: Whitelist-based class filtering in ObjectInputStream
sub_patterns.root_cause: The code uses a standard ObjectInputStream (or an ObjectInputFilter) that does not restrict which classes can be instantiated during deserialization, assuming all serialized data is safe.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Eliminate the use of ObjectInputStream entirely; instead parse the input as primitive fields (int, UTF strings, etc.) using DataInputStream or a custom protocol, or switch to a safe serialization format such as JSON with integrity verification.
sub_patterns.name: Replacement of native Java deserialization with safe data parsing
sub_patterns.root_cause: The code relies on Java's ObjectInputStream.readObject() to reconstruct objects from untrusted input, allowing instantiation of arbitrary classes.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Remove the Serializable interface from the vulnerable class, deprecate the class, or delete the entire deserialization code path so that no deserialization can occur.
sub_patterns.name: Elimination of serializable classes to prevent deserialization
sub_patterns.root_cause: The vulnerability exists because a class implements Serializable and is deserialized from untrusted sources without validation.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Introduce a check that the first deserialized class must be assignable to a specific expected type (e.g., ExprNodeDesc) and throw an exception if it is not.
sub_patterns.name: Type restriction for Kryo deserialization
sub_patterns.root_cause: The code uses Kryo to deserialize objects without any class allowlist, allowing instantiation of arbitrary classes from the classpath.

sub_patterns.name: Unrestricted Java deserialization without class filtering
